points: Autoscaling matches the capacity a service has to the demand it faces, by adding or removing copies or by resizing them.
New capacity takes minutes to arrive, so a good rule grows quickly, shrinks slowly and keeps a minimum and a maximum.
Google's Autopilot cuts the gap between reserved and used resources by setting task counts and limits from usage history.
MongoDB forecasts demand that scaling cannot change, and trusts a forecast only where its recent accuracy has been good.
In production MongoDB scales up on predictions and leaves scaling down to the reactive rule. The post calls this first version conservative.
